items.title: Secret documents show 'horrifying' traces of horse meat in food
items.description: Government documents show hundreds of businesses operating in Australia have breached food safety laws, with one politician warning "you could be eating a minced horse".

items.title: Live: Challenger Carroll arrives for vote as Victorian premier tipped to lose
items.description: Premier Jacinta Allan is facing a challenge for leadership of the Victorian Labor Party from her deputy Ben Carroll. Follow our live coverage.

items.title: Science and politics collide in fraught puberty blockers debate
items.description: The fierce debate over puberty blockers has become a collision of science and politics. To try to address a fractured consensus, the federal government is attempting to lay the groundwork for a national standard.

items.title: Trump tips the balance towards China in trade war
items.description: China has the market sewn up in everything from solar panels to battery manufacturing and wind turbines. And now it is challenging America's commanding role in technology.

items.title: Salmon farming transformed Norway. Now it's facing the consequences
items.description: Norway's salmon industry is a global behemoth 18 times the size of Tasmania's. But the country's success holds a warning for Australia.

items.title: How an accident changed the path of a grieving Angus Taylor's life
items.description: The Liberal leader opens about a balcony fall that left him with a broken back and altered the course of his life.

items.title: Twice named and shamed builder accused of leaving customers out of pocket
items.description: Unregistered builder Steve Preston has been operating in New South Wales after falling foul of authorities in Western Australia and Queensland.

items.title: Live: Australia claims first athletics gold, Dolphins dominating once more
items.description: Australia is enjoying another wildly successful day at the Commonwealth Games, with Rose Davies claiming her nation's first athletics gold and the Dolphins sweeping the medals in two events in the pool.

items.title: Australia should brace for war impact to get worse, Treasury warns
items.description: The federal government is yet to reveal whether it will extend the fuel excise discount, which is set to expire this week.

items.title: Live: ASX to open lower as the price of oil plunges
items.description: The Australian share market is set to open lower as the price of oil plunges more than 9 per cent. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Live: Shadow treasurer indicates Coalition support for new WA oil refinery
items.description: Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson indicates the Coalition will support the construction of a new oil refinery in Western Australia. Follow live.

items.title: Influencers pushing 'ideal of masculinity' drive male eating disorders
items.description: About 365,000 men across Australia are living with an eating disorder, but they face a system still dismissing them.

items.title: What to expect from antisemitism royal commission in coming weeks
items.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion is continuing in Sydney, with witnesses to give evidence about ways to improve education and training to prevent hate.

items.title: Twin tragedies leave community, nursing colleagues in shock
items.description: The car crash death of mother-of-two Elaine Gee and the stabbing of another woman will send "ripples" through the Tasmanian community, a family violence support service says.

items.title: Young buyers and sellers 'on the hunt' for second-hand clothing
items.description: Resale app users are balancing convenience with overconsumption in the second-hand fashion conversation.

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Your challenge in the ABC Places quiz is to work out the location of 10 photos from around the world. Be warned; we might try to trick you.

items.title: Boycotts and withdrawn funding 'part and parcel' of working in arts today
items.description: After the 2026 edition was subjected to political, community and commercial pressures, the Biennale of Sydney has announced a new artistic director: Singaporean curator Low Kee Hong.

items.title: The Utopia-style regulations holding Australia back from building homes
items.description: A new report from the Productivity Commission has called on governments to embrace a "build mindset" to make housing more affordable.

items.title: Warnings consumers 'the fall guy' if data centres soak up spare power supply
items.description: Consumers should brace for hefty increases in the cost of generating electricity as data centres suck up vast quantities of power faster than new plants can be built, experts say.

items.title: Search resumes for missing baby off South East SA coast
items.description: SA Police hold grave fears for the safety of a baby missing after the bodies of a woman and toddler were recovered in waters off Port MacDonnell.

items.title: Carly Simon refuses to be defined by Parkinson's diagnosis
items.description: Singer Carly Simon has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and is releasing a new album, Comes in Waves, in August.

items.title: Facial recognition could be your new ticket to the footy
items.description: Facial recognition technology is being used as an alternative form of ticketing, but some experts are concerned it could open the door to the data being used for more than just event entry.

items.title: 'Immediately I was homeless': The financial reality victim-survivors face
items.description: Rising living costs and housing insecurity are reshaping the experience of leaving domestic violence. Nicole Yade understands this experience firsthand.

items.title: Bill Oddie, member of The Goodies comedy series, dead at 85
items.description: British actor, comedian and broadcaster Bill Oddie, best known to Australian audiences as a member of the 1970s comedy trio The Goodies, has died aged 85, his agent has announced.

items.title: Lack of child care creates skills shortages as bush mums leave work
items.description: Looking at her young daughters, Emily McPhee hopes they will never have to choose between a career and raising a family in the bush.
